title: Kissed Kenyan Emmentaler Cheese Gratin
description: A nutty, chewy, and comforting Kenyan-inspired Emmentaler cheese gratin that's perfect for a lazy Sunday. The tandoor oven adds a unique smoky flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Emmentaler cheese
ingredients.notes: A type of Swiss cheese with a nutty flavor.

ingredients.name: Tandoor oven-roasted potatoes
ingredients.notes: Thinly sliced potatoes roasted in a tandoor oven until crispy.

ingredients.name: Onion
ingredients.notes: Chopped onion adds a sweet and savory flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Minced garlic adds depth to the Emmentaler cheese sauce.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley
ingredients.notes: Chopped parsley adds a fresh and herby flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Chopped cilantro adds a bright and citrusy flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Coconut oil
ingredients.notes: Used for saut4ing the onion and garlic.

ingredients.name: Black pepper
ingredients.notes: Adds a touch of heat to the dish.

ingredients.name: Paprika
ingredients.notes: Adds a smoky and slightly sweet flavor to the dish.

ingredients.name: Chili flakes
ingredients.notes: Adds a touch of heat to the dish.

instructions: Tandoor oven-roast the potatoes until crispy, about 20-25 minutes.
S15ut1e the chopped onion in coconut oil until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and cook for an additional 1-2 minutes, until fragrant.
In a separate saucepan, melt the Emmentaler cheese over low heat, stirring occasionally.
Add the roasted potatoes, chopped onion, and garlic to the cheese sauce and stir until combined.
Season the dish with salt, black pepper, paprika, and chili flakes.
Transfer the mixture to a baking dish and top with chopped parsley and cilantro.
Bake in a preheated oven at 37515F (19015C) for 20-25 minutes, until golden brown and bubbly.
Garnish with additional parsley and cilantro, if desired.
Cover and refrigerate any leftovers for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months.
